steps.intent: France’s objective is to renew UNIFIL for twelve months while preserving the resolution 1701 framework, anchoring the mandate in the November 2024 ceasefire, and supporting Lebanon’s 7 August 2025 decision to assert State authority and disarm armed groups. The most difficult negotiations will likely concern explicit language on Hezbollah’s disarmament, the characterization of Israeli strikes and continuing Israeli presence, and any attempts to narrow UNIFIL’s freedom of movement or introduce a mandate review. France expects broad support for a twelve-month renewal but must manage possible abstentions from Russia and China and concerns from the United States and Israel over the balance of the text.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of UNIFIL and Lebanon's sovereignty and territorial integrity, but the current draft remains too weak on Israeli violations. We ask the penholder to include an explicit condemnation of Israeli airstrikes, incursions and violations of Lebanese airspace and territorial waters, together with a clear demand for immediate and complete withdrawal from all Lebanese territory. We also need the language on the Government of Lebanon's 7 August decision to be anchored in Lebanese sovereignty and in the end of the occupation, not imposed from outside.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of UNIFIL and the Council's support for Lebanon's sovereignty and stability. We ask the penholder to ensure that the Lebanese Government's plan is implemented through political dialogue and national consensus, with full respect for Lebanon's sovereignty and without external interference. Support to the LAF should be at the request and with the consent of the Government of Lebanon, and UNIFIL's safety and TCC consultations must be strengthened. We can join consensus with these adjustments.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the renewal of UNIFIL and the balanced draft, which rightly centres resolution 1701 (2006) and Lebanese state authority. We would like the operative text to give clearer effect to the 27 November 2024 ceasefire, including a defined timeline for Israeli withdrawal, and to make explicit that all armed groups, including Hezbollah, must disarm. We could also accept a new operative paragraph on humanitarian access and the safe, voluntary return of displaced persons.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the renewal of UNIFIL's mandate and the balanced framework in the French draft. We would ask the penholder to strengthen OP4 by anchoring disarmament in a comprehensive national process consistent with the Taif Accords and resolution 1701, and to reinforce UNIFIL's freedom of movement and the inviolability of UN premises in OP6. A minor addition on Lebanese airspace violations would also help reflect the sovereignty concerns we share.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks France for the consultative process and supports renewal of UNIFIL's mandate and the text's emphasis on resolution 1701, Lebanese sovereignty and the 27 November ceasefire. To strengthen the text, we ask that OP4 explicitly frame implementation of the 7 August decision as Lebanese-led and in full respect of Lebanon's sovereignty, and that a new operative paragraph require safe, timely and unhindered humanitarian access and facilitate safe, voluntary and dignified returns. We would also welcome minor reporting additions on humanitarian access and violations affecting children. Guyana is ready to work constructively toward consensus.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the renewal of UNIFIL's mandate and the draft's emphasis on resolution 1701 and Lebanese sovereignty. We ask the penholder to add an explicit operative condemnation of Israeli airstrikes and incursions and a call for their immediate cessation, and to make clear in OP4 that implementation of Lebanon's plan is Lebanese-led, in accordance with its Constitution and free from external interference. We also request that OP9 refer to full and timely consultation with troop-contributing countries on any changes affecting UNIFIL personnel and operations.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of UNIFIL and welcomes France's balanced draft. We ask that Lebanese leadership and consent be made explicit in the provisions on disarmament and international support to the Lebanese Armed Forces, consistent with Lebanon's sovereignty. We would also welcome an operative call for the safe and voluntary return of displaced persons and unimpeded humanitarian access; with these adjustments we can support the text.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks France for the balanced text and supports the renewal of UNIFIL’s mandate. As a troop-contributing country, we ask that OP8 explicitly require reporting on the safety and security of UNIFIL personnel and on impediments to their freedom of movement, and that OP9 ensure troop-contributing countries are kept fully informed of security measures affecting their personnel. With these technical improvements, we can support the draft.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the renewal of UNIFIL and welcomes the balanced thrust of the French text. We need an explicit reference to Israeli violations of Lebanese airspace, including military overflights of Beirut, as we have consistently underlined. The 7 August decision should be treated as a sovereign Lebanese process and linked to Israel's withdrawal, and support to the Lebanese Armed Forces must be coordinated with the Lebanese Government.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of UNIFIL's mandate and welcomes France's balanced draft. We would ask the penholder to strengthen operative language on humanitarian access in OP6 and to make OP8 reporting capture obstacles to access and to the safe, voluntary and dignified return of displaced persons. These changes reflect Sierra Leone's consistent emphasis on protection of civilians and humanitarian imperatives.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the renewal of UNIFIL’s mandate and the balanced approach of the draft. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP6 with an explicit obligation to ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, and to add reporting on obstacles to humanitarian access and the protection of children in OP8. We also believe OP7 should recall that attacks on UN peacekeepers may constitute war crimes and require prompt, independent investigations.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of UNIFIL and the overall balance of the French draft. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP3 on Israel's complete withdrawal and OP4 by anchoring the disarmament process firmly in Lebanese sovereignty and a Lebanese-led process. We also seek a clearer condemnation in OP7 of continuing Israeli violations of Lebanese sovereignty, while retaining condemnation of all violations and attacks against UNIFIL.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK supports the renewal and the overall balance of the text. We would like the disarmament provisions to name Hezbollah explicitly and to call on all States, including Iran, to stop arms supplies to Hezbollah and other armed groups. We also ask that OP6 reflect the preamble by ensuring UNIFIL's unrestricted access, and that reporting cover arms smuggling. These changes would make the mandate more credible and implementation more reciprocal.
messages.United States of America: The United States can support a one-year extension, but the draft must be rebalanced so that it does not single out Israel while treating Hezbollah’s armed presence and attacks as background. The 7 August Lebanese decision must be turned into an operative demand for disarmament, including Hezbollah, with clear reporting on obstruction of UNIFIL. We are prepared to work on compromise language that preserves UNIFIL’s freedom of movement and supports the Lebanese Armed Forces.

steps.summary: France has revised the text to meet U.S. red lines on balance and disarmament while retaining strong Lebanese sovereignty language and explicit condemnation of Israeli violations in operative paragraph 9. The text should command broad support, with Algeria and Russia possible abstentions over the placement and strength of certain airspace and withdrawal language.

messages.Algeria: We welcome the strengthened withdrawal language in OP3 and the explicit condemnation of Israeli violations in OP9. To support the text, Algeria asks that OP4 link implementation of the 7 August decision to the complete withdrawal of Israeli forces and restoration of Lebanese sovereignty, and that OP9 condemn all violations in the strongest terms, as OP5 does for Hezbollah. We also oppose singling out Iran in OP6; the Council should address arms transfers to non-State actors without targeting one Member State.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of UNIFIL's mandate and appreciates the penholder's acceptance of our earlier proposals on Lebanese ownership, consent, Israeli airspace violations and TCC consultation. We request two final adjustments to keep the text balanced and impartial: OP6 should not single out any State, and OP11's reporting language should refer to obstruction by any party. With these changes, China is ready to support the resolution.
messages.Denmark: Denmark welcomes revision 1 and the incorporation of our previous requests on OP3, OP4 and OP10. We believe the text provides a balanced basis for renewing UNIFIL, supporting full implementation of resolution 1701 and the 27 November 2024 ceasefire, and addressing violations and humanitarian needs. Denmark will support the draft and urges all Council members to vote in favour and to focus on implementation.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the revised draft. We welcome the incorporation of our earlier points on Lebanese airspace, a Lebanese-led national process for disarmament, and UNIFIL’s freedom of movement and the inviolability of UN premises. The text strikes a necessary balance: it upholds Lebanon’s sovereignty, calls for full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006) and the 27 November 2024 ceasefire, and addresses violations by all parties. Greece is ready to vote in favour and encourages all Council members to support adoption.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks France for incorporating our earlier concerns on a Lebanese-led process, humanitarian access and return, and reporting. We can support the current text as balanced and consistent with Lebanon’s sovereignty and UNIFIL’s mandate. We encourage all parties to implement the ceasefire and resolution 1701 (2006) fully, and urge continued close consultation with troop-contributing countries.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the renewal of UNIFIL and welcomes the balanced language in OP9 and the TCC consultation in OP12. We remain concerned about singling out Iran in OP6 and about one-sided reporting language in OP11; these amendments would keep the Council's approach balanced and preserve Lebanon's sovereignty. With these changes, Pakistan can support the text.
messages.Panama: Panama welcomes the revised text and the incorporation of its earlier concerns on Lebanese leadership, consent for support to the Lebanese Armed Forces, and the safe, voluntary and dignified return of displaced persons. The delegation supports a consensus adoption and urges all parties to fully implement resolution 1701 (2006), the 27 November 2024 ceasefire and the Lebanese Government’s decision of 7 August 2025.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the revised text and appreciates the penholder’s incorporation of our proposals on UNIFIL reporting and TCC consultation and information-sharing. As a troop-contributing country, we regard the provisions on peacekeeper safety, freedom of movement and full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006) as essential. We will vote in favour and encourage all Council members to do the same.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation continues to support a balanced renewal of UNIFIL and appreciates the penholder's partial incorporation of our earlier comments, including moving airspace violations to OP9 and adding Lebanese constitutional procedures in OP4. However, the text remains unbalanced: OP4 must link the disarmament process to the parallel withdrawal of Israeli forces and cessation of Israeli violations, and OP6 must not single out Iran. We ask the penholder to reflect these changes so that the Council can maintain unity in renewing UNIFIL's mandate.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier concerns on humanitarian access and reporting on obstacles to access and to the safe, voluntary and dignified return of displaced persons. We support the current text and encourage all Council members to unite behind it ahead of the vote.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks France for its balanced revision and for accepting our proposals on humanitarian access, accountability for attacks against UN peacekeepers, and reporting on children and vulnerable groups. We support the current text as it stands. We call for its full implementation, with particular emphasis on protecting civilians, ensuring UNIFIL’s safety and freedom of movement, and upholding accountability under international law.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of UNIFIL and welcomes the penholder's efforts to strengthen the text, including the balanced condemnation in OP9. We still ask that OP3 explicitly require the unconditional withdrawal of Israeli forces from all Lebanese territory, consistent with Lebanon's sovereignty and resolution 1701 (2006). With that amendment, Somalia can support the draft.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks France for the revised text and welcomes the incorporation of our key priorities: naming Hezbollah, addressing Iranian arms supplies, ensuring UNIFIL access, and reporting on arms smuggling. The draft strikes the right balance in supporting Lebanon’s sovereignty, UNIFIL’s mandate, and the full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006). We can support the text as it stands.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports renewing UNIFIL, but we cannot accept language that condemns Israeli self-defense actions or requires immediate Israeli withdrawal without conditions. We need OP3 to condition withdrawal on LAF deployment and Hezbollah’s disarmament, and OP9 to condemn Hezbollah attacks and call on all parties to cease violations rather than condemning Israeli airstrikes. We also ask that OP4 prevent any armed group from using ‘national consensus’ to block disarmament, and that OP6 make the arms-supply prohibition a demand, especially on Iran.

replies.Algeria: partially accepted: OP4 links disarmament with withdrawal, cessation of violations and restoration, and OP9 uses strongest-terms language for attacks and other violations; the immediate-withdrawal insertion is not included due the U.S. red line.
replies.China: accepted: OP6 no longer singles out Iran and OP11 refers to obstruction by any party.
replies.France: penholder: supports the revised text and incorporated balanced P5 compromises.
replies.Pakistan: partially accepted: OP6 no longer names Iran and OP11 is broadened to any party, but OP11 does not retain an explicit Hezbollah reference.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: OP4 now refers to all Lebanese parties in parallel with withdrawal and cessation of violations, and OP6 removes Iran and refers to unauthorized non-State actors without singling out a Member State.
replies.Somalia: rejected: 'unconditional' withdrawal is not included because OP3 conditions withdrawal on parallel LAF deployment and disarmament per the U.S. red line.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: no changes requested; the text retains Hezbollah accountability and arms-smuggling reporting.
replies.United States of America: partially accepted: OP3 and OP9 red lines are incorporated and OP4 prevents armed-group veto and OP6 is strengthened to 'Demands'; Iran is not singled out to maintain P5 unity.

steps.summary: France revised the draft to preserve UNIFIL renewal and resolution 1701 while accommodating the U.S. red lines on conditioned withdrawal and OP9 and removing the Iran-specific reference to protect P5 unity. The text balances Lebanese sovereignty, Hezbollah accountability and UNIFIL safety, and is expected to be adopted unanimously.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria’s priorities are Lebanese sovereignty, Israeli withdrawal and UNIFIL renewal; the draft partly accommodates its amendments and preserves the peacekeeping mandate, so Algeria supports it while registering concerns before the vote.
reasons.China: China supports renewing UNIFIL and a balanced implementation of resolution 1701, and its key textual concerns were accommodated. It therefore votes in favour while stressing Lebanese sovereignty, Israeli withdrawal, and UNIFIL safety.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark consistently supports UNIFIL, resolution 1701 (2006), and Lebanese sovereignty, and the draft aligns with its stated support from the last negotiation round. Denmark therefore votes in favour.
reasons.France: France is the penholder and has consistently supported UNIFIL renewal and full implementation of resolution 1701, Lebanese sovereignty, and the 2024 ceasefire. It will therefore vote in favour while explaining its support for the balanced obligations on all parties.
reasons.Greece: Greece had already indicated support and made no requests; the resolution aligns with its support for UNIFIL, Lebanese sovereignty, and a balanced implementation of resolution 1701. A supportive explanation of vote is consistent with Greece’s record on Lebanon and its role as a UNIFIL maritime contributor.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported UNIFIL renewals and Lebanon’s sovereignty, and the draft aligns with its prior positions. The last negotiation round recorded Guyana’s support with no requested changes.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan’s key requested change to OP6 was accepted, and the minor OP11 request was substantially addressed; voting in favour aligns with Pakistan’s support for Lebanese sovereignty, UNIFIL, and balanced implementation of resolution 1701. A pre-vote statement registers concerns about Israeli violations and peacekeeper safety while preserving support for the draft.
reasons.Panama: Panama had already indicated support with no requested changes; the draft aligns with its support for UNIFIL, resolution 1701, Lebanese sovereignty, and international law.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea is a UNIFIL troop contributor and has consistently supported balanced mandate renewals that reinforce resolution 1701, ceasefire implementation, and peacekeeper safety. The draft matches its earlier positions, and it requested no changes.
reasons.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation secured partial acceptance of its key amendments, sufficient to avoid a veto and maintain support for UNIFIL’s renewal, while registering reservations about unbalanced language. Its established policy favours preserving the Council’s unity on Lebanon and supporting the peacekeeping mandate.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently voted in favour of previous Lebanon-related Council texts and UNIFIL renewals, and this draft aligns with its support for Lebanese sovereignty, ceasefire implementation, protection of peacekeepers and humanitarian access.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia was listed as supporting the draft and made no requests; the text aligns with its consistent emphasis on UNIFIL, resolution 1701, civilian protection, Lebanese sovereignty and international law.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia’s priority is preserving UNIFIL and Lebanese sovereignty; despite the rejected wording on unconditional withdrawal, the draft advances core interests and aligns with its recent support for Lebanon-related consensus resolutions.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK consistently supports UNIFIL renewal and resolution 1701 implementation while strongly condemning Hizbullah and supporting Lebanese state authority, so it would vote in favour. A pre-vote explanation is appropriate to underline both Israel’s withdrawal obligations and Hizbullah’s disarmament and accountability.
reasons.United States of America: U.S. red lines on immediate Israeli withdrawal and false equivalence with Hezbollah were incorporated, and the text strongly condemns Hezbollah, backs LAF deployment and disarmament, and supports UNIFIL with implementation safeguards. The United States therefore votes yes and explains its vote before the vote.

before.Algeria: Algeria votes in favour of the renewal of UNIFIL’s mandate. We do so because the stability of Lebanon and the full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006) remain essential, and because UNIFIL continues to play a critical role in supporting the Lebanese Armed Forces and in monitoring and reporting violations. We welcome the text’s reaffirmation of Lebanon’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence, and its call for the full implementation of the 27 November 2024 ceasefire, including the full and complete withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory in parallel with the deployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces and the restoration of Lebanese sovereignty. We also support the Lebanese Government’s decision of 7 August 2025 to assert the authority and monopoly on the use of force of the Lebanese State over all Lebanese territory through a Lebanese-led process, free from external interference, and we stress that this must proceed in parallel with ending the Israeli occupation and all violations of Lebanese sovereignty. Algeria regrets that our amendment calling for an immediate, full and complete withdrawal of Israeli forces from all Lebanese territory was not retained, and we emphasize that all violations must be condemned equally, including Israeli violations of Lebanese airspace and territorial waters. We nevertheless vote in favour in support of Lebanon, UNIFIL and the cause of a just and lasting peace.
before.China: Mr. President, China will vote in favour of the draft resolution. The situation in Lebanon remains fragile, and the renewal of UNIFIL’s mandate is important for maintaining stability along the Blue Line and supporting the full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006) and the 27 November 2024 ceasefire agreement. We welcome that the penholder has taken on board China’s concerns in paragraphs 6 and 11. We stress that the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Lebanon must be fully respected. The ceasefire and relevant arrangements should be implemented in a balanced and synchronized manner, including the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory and the deployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces. All violations, including of Lebanese airspace, must cease. The question of armed groups and weapons in Lebanon should be addressed by the Lebanese people through an inclusive Lebanese-led political process, without external interference. The safety and security of UNIFIL personnel and troop-contributing countries must be guaranteed, and UNIFIL’s freedom of movement must be respected. China will continue to support Lebanon in safeguarding stability and sovereignty.
before.Denmark: Denmark will vote in favour of this resolution. We strongly support the renewal of UNIFIL’s mandate and the full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006) and the 27 November 2024 ceasefire. We underline the need for respect for Lebanon’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, the withdrawal of Israeli forces, the deployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces throughout southern Lebanon, the disarmament of armed groups including Hezbollah, and the safety and freedom of movement of UNIFIL personnel. We also call on all parties to protect civilians and ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The Council cannot allow the cessation of hostilities to be eroded or the framework of resolution 1701 (2006) to be abandoned. The renewal of UNIFIL for twelve months is essential to support the Lebanese Armed Forces, monitor violations, protect civilians and create the conditions for the full and complete withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory in parallel with the disarmament and dismantlement of armed groups, including Hezbollah. France stresses that all attacks against peacekeepers are unacceptable, that all parties must respect the Blue Line and Lebanese sovereignty, and that the Lebanese authorities must be able to exercise the monopoly on the use of force throughout their territory. We call on the Council to speak with one voice in support of Lebanon’s stability, sovereignty and territorial integrity and in support of the safety and effectiveness of UNIFIL.
before.Greece: Greece will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We thank France for its efforts to consolidate the Council’s support for Lebanon’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, unity and political independence. Greece firmly supports the extension of UNIFIL’s mandate and the full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006) and the 27 November 2024 ceasefire agreement. We stress the need for the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory, the deployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces throughout southern Lebanon, and the disarmament of all armed groups through a Lebanese-led political process free from external interference. All parties must respect the Blue Line, including Lebanese airspace and territorial waters, and ensure the safety, security and freedom of movement of UNIFIL personnel. We also call for unhindered humanitarian access and the safe, voluntary and dignified return of displaced persons. Greece will continue to support Lebanon’s stability and the Lebanese Armed Forces’ ability to assume their responsibilities.
before.Guyana: Guyana votes in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of UNIFIL’s mandate, the full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006) and the 27 November 2024 ceasefire, and the restoration of Lebanese sovereignty throughout Lebanon. We stress that all parties must comply with international humanitarian law, protect civilians and humanitarian and United Nations personnel, ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, and respect the Blue Line, including Lebanese airspace. We further urge that Lebanon’s authority be asserted through a Lebanese-led political process, without external interference, and that implementation of the 7 August 2025 decision proceed in a manner that preserves Lebanon’s stability and sovereignty. Guyana remains committed to supporting UNIFIL and the people of Lebanon.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the penholder for its efforts to accommodate the concerns raised in the negotiations. We welcome the revisions to paragraph 6, which avoid singling out any Member State, and the broadening of paragraph 11 to cover obstruction by any party. Pakistan will vote in favour of this draft because it reaffirms Lebanon’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence and extends UNIFIL’s mandate, which remains essential for stability. At the same time, we stress that the implementation of resolution 1701 (2006) and the ceasefire must be balanced and comprehensive. Israeli violations of Lebanese airspace and territorial integrity, as well as attacks against civilians and United Nations personnel, must cease, and all parties must respect the Blue Line. The safety, security and freedom of movement of UNIFIL personnel, including from troop-contributing countries, must be fully ensured, and troop-contributing countries must be kept closely informed. We also underline the need for humanitarian access and the safe, voluntary and dignified return of displaced persons. Pakistan’s support for this text is grounded in our consistent position in favour of Lebanon’s sovereignty and regional peace and stability.
before.Panama: Panama votes in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of UNIFIL’s mandate and the full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006), including respect for Lebanon’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory, the deployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces, and the disarmament of armed groups in accordance with the decisions of the Government of Lebanon. We underline the need for all parties to respect the Blue Line, protect civilians and United Nations personnel, ensure humanitarian access, and pursue a permanent ceasefire through diplomatic means. Panama remains committed to international law and to a stable, sovereign and independent Lebanon.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks France for its efforts as penholder and will vote in favour of this draft resolution. As a long-standing troop-contributing country to UNIFIL, my delegation strongly supports the renewal of UNIFIL’s mandate until 31 August 2026, which provides the continuity and predictability needed for the mission to implement its mandate under resolution 1701 (2006). We call on all parties to fully implement the 27 November 2024 ceasefire, respect the Blue Line, ensure the safety and security of peacekeepers, and facilitate safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. We also encourage a Lebanese-led process to assert State authority and the monopoly on the use of force, in full respect for Lebanon’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We note that a number of our concerns were taken into account: OP4 now refers to all Lebanese parties and links the cessation of armed activity to the full implementation of the ceasefire, including the complete withdrawal of Israeli forces and the cessation of all violations, while OP6 no longer singles out a Member State. At the same time, we remain concerned by the draft’s persistent one-sided emphasis on Hezbollah. A sustainable settlement in Lebanon cannot be imposed by force or by ignoring Israeli violations of Lebanese sovereignty, territorial integrity and airspace. We call for the strict implementation of resolution 1701 (2006), the 27 November 2024 ceasefire and UNIFIL’s mandate, with full respect for Lebanon’s sovereignty and without external interference. UNIFIL remains a stabilizing factor, and its mandate should not be undermined by attempts to use this resolution as a pretext for escalation.
before.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone votes in favour of this draft resolution. We support the extension of UNIFIL’s mandate and reaffirm Lebanon’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity within its internationally recognized borders. Sierra Leone calls for the full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006), the 27 November 2024 ceasefire and the decision of the Government of Lebanon of 7 August 2025, and urges all parties to cease violations, protect civilians and United Nations personnel, ensure safe humanitarian access, and support the safe, voluntary and dignified return of displaced persons. We also stress the importance of the safety, security and freedom of movement of UNIFIL personnel and troop-contributing countries’ full involvement in decisions affecting their personnel. Sierra Leone will continue to support Lebanon’s stability and the full restoration of the Lebanese State’s authority throughout its territory.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks France for its work on this text and will vote in favour. We support the extension of UNIFIL’s mandate as a vital stabilizing factor and stress the need for full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006) and the 27 November 2024 ceasefire. We remain deeply concerned by continuing violations and escalation, and we call on all parties to respect the Blue Line, protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, and guarantee the safety, security and freedom of movement of UNIFIL personnel. We also underline that Lebanon’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence must be respected, and that the disarmament of armed groups should proceed through a Lebanese-led process and in parallel with the full withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory. Slovenia remains committed to accountability for all violations and to the full and faithful implementation of this resolution.
before.Somalia: Mr. President, Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so to support the renewal of UNIFIL, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Lebanon, and the safety of peacekeepers and civilians. At the same time, my delegation reiterates that Israeli forces must withdraw completely from Lebanese territory and that all parties must respect the Blue Line, resolution 1701 (2006) and their obligations under international law. We call for balanced implementation and accountability for all violations.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr. President, the United Kingdom welcomes the renewal of UNIFIL’s mandate and thanks France for its efforts to bring the Council together on this important text. The United Kingdom will vote in favour. UNIFIL’s role remains essential, and the mission must have the freedom of movement and access it needs to implement its mandate safely. We remain committed to the full implementation of resolution 1701 and the 27 November ceasefire arrangements, including the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory and the deployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces throughout the south. We strongly support the Lebanese Government’s decision of 7 August to assert the State’s monopoly on the use of force and to disarm all armed groups, including Hizbullah. Hizbullah’s continued attacks and military activity are unacceptable and undermine Lebanon’s sovereignty and stability. At the same time, all parties must respect the Blue Line, cease violations, protect civilians and UN personnel, and ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. The United Kingdom calls on all States to prevent the supply of arms to unauthorized non-State actors and to support the Lebanese State in taking control of its territory in accordance with its obligations. We urge the parties to de-escalate and return to a political process that delivers lasting security for both Lebanon and Israel.
before.United States of America: Mr. President, the United States will vote in favor of this resolution. The Council must speak clearly in support of Lebanon’s sovereignty and the Lebanese Armed Forces, and in support of the full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006) and the November 2024 ceasefire. We welcome the Council’s endorsement of the Lebanese Government’s 7 August decision to assert a monopoly on the use of force and to disarm all armed groups, including Hezbollah. We also welcome the clear condemnation of Hezbollah’s attacks and the demand that all States prevent arms transfers to unauthorized non-State actors. At the same time, implementation must be balanced and sequenced: Israeli forces should withdraw as the Lebanese Armed Forces deploy and as Hezbollah and other armed groups disarm. UNIFIL must have the freedom of movement and security it needs, and its mandate must not become a permanent substitute for the Lebanese State’s responsibilities. The United States remains committed to Lebanon’s security, stability, and sovereignty.

after.France:
Thank you, Mr. President.

France welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution. As penholder, France thanks all Council members for their constructive engagement and their commitment to Lebanon’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity.

This unanimous vote sends a clear message: the framework of resolution 1701 (2006) and the ceasefire of 27 November 2024 must be fully respected and implemented. The Council cannot allow the cessation of hostilities to be eroded. We call on all parties to respect the Blue Line, to cease all violations — including violations of Lebanese airspace — and to ensure the safety, security and freedom of movement of UNIFIL personnel. Attacks against peacekeepers are unacceptable and must be investigated and accounted for.

The full and complete withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory must proceed in parallel with the deployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces throughout southern Lebanon and with the disarmament and dismantlement of armed groups, including Hezbollah, through a Lebanese-led political process, in full respect for Lebanon’s sovereignty. France supports the Lebanese Government’s decision of 7 August 2025 to assert the State’s monopoly on the use of force over all Lebanese territory by the end of 2025, and calls on all Lebanese parties to cooperate with the Lebanese Armed Forces.

France will remain actively engaged with its partners to support Lebanon, its Armed Forces and its people. We underline the need for safe and unimpeded humanitarian access and for the safe, voluntary and dignified return of displaced persons. The Council must now ensure that this resolution is implemented in full. France will continue to follow the situation closely and stands ready to work with all members to that end.
after.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation voted in favour of the adopted resolution. We did so because it extends UNIFIL’s mandate and retains an important link between the cessation of armed activity and the full implementation of the 27 November 2024 ceasefire, including the complete withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory and the cessation of all violations. At the same time, we regret that the text continues to place a one-sided emphasis on Hezbollah while failing to reflect with due clarity Israel’s continued violations of Lebanese sovereignty, territorial integrity and airspace. A stable settlement in Lebanon cannot be imposed by force or through external interference. The disarmament of armed groups must proceed through a Lebanese-led political process, in parallel with Israel’s withdrawal and the deployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces, and must not serve as a pretext for military pressure. We call for strict implementation of resolution 1701 (2006), the ceasefire arrangements and UNIFIL’s mandate, with full respect for Lebanon’s sovereignty. UNIFIL personnel must be safe and have freedom of movement, and all parties must protect civilians and ensure unimpeded humanitarian access. The Russian Federation will continue to monitor implementation and will oppose any attempt to use this resolution to escalate the situation or to undermine Lebanon’s sovereignty.
